subject: PeregrineHealth - SIG: forensic freeze & retrieval API request
messages:
From: Sarah Nolan <sarah.nolan@peregrinehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Legal Team <legal@peregrinehealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T08:23:00-05:00
Subject: Request: temporary forensic freeze + SIG evidence access

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this — Peregrine Health is preparing for an upcoming SIG assessment (request received by our procurement team) and we have two asks we need to validate with Redwood before we sign:

1) Short-term forensic freeze: we need a way to preserve tenant-scoped debug/audit traces beyond your default ephemeral window for a 90-day investigation window. This must create an immutable snapshot (read-only) and be auditable.

2) Retrieval / eDiscovery access: auditors will want periodic exports (manifest + signed hash) and the ability to pull specific sessions via an API or S3 export. Ideally we can generate short-lived links and have RBAC for which Peregrine engineers can request exports.

Can you confirm whether Redwood supports this pattern, typical lead times, and what the evidence package looks like (signed proof-of-delete, manifest, chain-of-custody notes, etc.)? Also share any cost guidance — procurement will need an estimate.

Attaching the SIG question subset we received and an SSO diagram for context.

Thanks,
Sarah Nolan
Director, Security & Compliance
Peregrine Health

Attachments: sig_questions.pdf (application/pdf), sso-diagram.png (image/png)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Nolan <sarah.nolan@peregrinehealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-10T12:05:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary forensic freeze + SIG evidence access

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and the SIG slice. Short answer: yes, we can support an auditable short-term forensic freeze and programmatic retrieval. Below is a concise summary and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the evidence bundle and timeline.

Summary of options (what Redwood can provide):
- Forensic hold (tenant-level snapshot): create point-in-time immutable snapshots of session logs and ephemeral caches. Default retention for ephemeral traces is 30 days; forensic holds can extend immutability for a configured window (30-365 days).
- Export modes: a) Bulk S3 export (encrypted, KMS-wrapped) with manifest + SHA256 checksums and signed timestamps; b) eDiscovery API that returns session bundles and presigned URLs for selective retrieval; c) Secure evidence zip with signed manifest delivered to a Redwood customer portal.
- Audit trail: every freeze/request/export is recorded in our audit logs (who requested, job id, hashes, KMS key id). We can provide a signed statement (HSM-backed signature) over the manifest for SIG/C A I Q evidence.
- Proof-of-delete: when the hold window expires and data is removed, we provide a deletion certificate (manifest of deleted objects + signed proof).

Questions to scope cost & timeline:
1) Target retention window for the freeze (you mentioned 90 days; confirm 90 vs. 180).
2) Expected export cadence (one-time at snapshot creation, weekly, or on-demand by auditors?).
3) Who needs retrieval RBAC (roles vs email addresses) — do you prefer scoped API keys or SSO-based short-lived tokens?
4) Is end-to-end FIPS/HSM requirement for the signed artifact required?

Lead times and cost guidance:
- Administrative lead time: 3 business days to enable an account-level forensic hold configuration (short window) once SOW/Addendum signed.
- Snapshot generation/export: snapshot job typically completes within 2–6 hours for the tenant depending on volume; exports delivered within the same window.
- Evidence packaging & HSM signing: add 1–2 business days for HSM-backed signatures and the supporting affidavit.
- Approximate POC cost: baseline retention extension + export tooling is $2,500 one-time + $0.15/GB exported (ballpark, will finalize in SOW).

I attached a template we usually send to customers that lists the exact artifacts we produce; it should help you check boxes for SIG/CAIQ. If you confirm answers to the four questions above we can produce a formal SOW addendum and a sample evidence package.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence-pack-template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: temporary forensic freeze + retrieval API access

Hi all — adding technical details so Peregrine has what auditors will expect. (Putting this reply in Karthik's thread for traceability.)

Technical implementation notes:
- Snapshot semantics: we create an immutable snapshot by sealing the KV cache + request traces into a content-addressed store. Snapshots are write-once; only metadata is mutable (status, export jobs).
- Exports & API:
  * GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/evidence-snapshots -> lists snapshots with signed manifest URLs
  * POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/evidence-snapshots/{snapshot_id}/export -> kicks off S3 export, returns job id and presigned S3 location(s)
  * GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/evidence-snapshots/{snapshot_id}/session/{session_id} -> returns zipped session bundle (with SHA256 and signature)
- RBAC & access patterns: we support SSO (OIDC) with short-lived access tokens + scoped API keys for automation. We recommend SSO for auditor access with role scoping (auditor_readonly).
- Cryptography & KMS: exports are encrypted with customer-specific KMS when on Dedicated/Private. For hosted customers we use our HSM-wrapped signing key; we can add FIPS attestation on request (adds lead time).
- Immutable retention policy: the hold is enforced server-side; deletion jobs are blocked until expiry and all access is captured in audit logs.

Operational playbook:
- Enable forensic hold -> snapshot occurs (t0) -> run verification job (t+1h) -> provide signed manifest to customer -> allow selective retrieval via API -> when hold expires, run purge job + produce deletion certificate (signed).

Operational notes for procurement: we can include a one-off retention addendum in the enrollment SOW. If Peregrine needs contractual SLA for snapshot completion/time-to-export we will price that in the addendum.

Happy to walk through the API and demo an export job; recommend a 30-minute call with your auditors to validate the artifacts.

- Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

- Export cadence: initial export at snapshot creation + on-demand pulls by auditors (we will supply a small auditor roster).
- Access: SSO-based auditor role (auditor_readonly) + one scoped API key for our SOC team.

Procurement asks that Redwood provide an cost estimate line itemized as: one-time retention addendum, per-GB export fees, optional SLA for snapshot completion. Our legal team will also need a sample deletion certificate to review.

Can we get a 30-minute technical call with Marcus and a short sample manifest/example signed deletion certificate before Friday 2026-11-13? Once we have that we'll route the addendum through procurement (deal PD-8421).
